text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Workup for medical causes of low mood and weight loss: blood count, metabolic panel, calcium, albumin, TSH, vitamin B12, and folate; MoCA cognitive screen; medication review (stop the over-the-counter diphenhydramine sleep aid); dental examination; age-appropriate cancer screening confirmed up to date
  • Suicide-risk assessment and collaborative safety plan: warning signs, coping steps, people to contact, the clinic number, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; medicines kept by her maid; safety reviewed at every visit
  • Geriatric psychiatry consultation to confirm the diagnosis, review grief, cognition, and safety, and advise on antidepressant choice and psychotherapy for an older adult
  • Shared decision on treatment: combined interpersonal psychotherapy, focused on grief, and a second-generation antidepressant; she chose sertraline, starting at 25 mg for a week, then 50 mg, with a review every two to four weeks and a dose increase if she is not in remission by about twelve weeks; no tricyclics, paroxetine, or other strongly anticholinergic drugs
  • Weekly individual interpersonal psychotherapy with the clinic psychologist, in private sessions at the end of the day, for about 16 sessions
  • Sleep: stop diphenhydramine; cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (sleep window, stimulus control, a fixed rising time, no long naps, and worry time early in the evening); no benzodiazepines, Z-drugs, or sedating antihistamines
  • Nutrition: three small meals and two snacks a day, an oral nutrition supplement twice a day, weight at every visit, and a dental review for the painful partial denture
  • Falls: Timed Up and Go and orthostatic blood pressure now and again if an antidepressant is started, since SSRIs raise fall risk in older adults; home safety review with her staff; an exercise class for balance and strength
  • Measurement-based care: PHQ-9 at every visit and at least monthly and GDS-15 monthly; if an SSRI is started, a sodium check two to four weeks later; continue any treatment that works for at least six to twelve months after remission
  • Privacy: chart access restricted to her care team, appointments at the end of the clinic day, results given in person, and nothing released without her written consent

resource.title: Elizabeth I synthetic care plan
resource.description: Evaluate and treat major depression in a 69-year-old woman who holds a demanding lifelong public office, after several bereavements, following the 2019 APA depression guideline (combined second-generation antidepressant and interpersonal psychotherapy for older adults), the 2022 VA/DoD MDD guideline, the CMID depression monograph, and the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria: a presenting problem of low mood, poor sleep, poor intake, and weight loss worked up for medical causes (blood count, metabolic panel, calcium, albumin, thyroid, vitamin B12, folate, a cognitive screen, and a medication review that stops an anticholinergic sleep aid); PHQ-9 and GDS-15 for measurement-based care; suicide-risk assessment with a passive death wish, a safety plan, and the 988 Lifeline, reviewed at every visit; sertraline started low and raised slowly, with a sodium check for SSRI-related hyponatremia; CBT for insomnia rather than hypnotics; nutrition, dental care, and weight; falls prevention while starting an SSRI; grief distinguished from depression; and the privacy of a public figure.
